text: For a one-dimensional map x_{n+1} = f(x_n), a fixed point x* is linearly stable when:
explanation: Near x*, perturbations are scaled by f'(x*) at each step, so |f'(x*)| < 1 contracts them (stable) while |f'(x*)| > 1 repels them (unstable). The value |f'(x*)| = 1 is the marginal case where a bifurcation typically occurs. f(x*) = 0 is unrelated, since a fixed point satisfies f(x*) = x*.
